text: 石の上にも三年
translit: ishi no ue ni mo san nen
en: Even on a stone, three years
meaning: Sit on a cold stone for three years and it will warm — patience and persistence turn even the most uncomfortable start into success.

text: 七転び八起き
translit: nanakorobi yaoki
en: Fall seven times, stand up eight
meaning: Resilience matters more than never failing: get back up one more time than you fall.

text: 急がば回れ
translit: isogaba maware
en: If you are in a hurry, go the long way round
meaning: The safe, careful route is usually the fastest to arrive by — haste makes waste.

text: 出る杭は打たれる
translit: deru kuri wa utareru
en: The nail that sticks out gets hammered down
meaning: Standing out from the group invites criticism — a warning about conformity in society.

text: 千里之行，始於足下
translit: qiān lǐ zhī xíng, shǐ yú zú xià
en: A journey of a thousand miles begins beneath the foot
meaning: Any great undertaking starts with a single first step. Attributed to Laozi, the Tao Te Ching.

text: 熟能生巧
translit: shú néng shēng qiǎo
en: Familiarity breeds skill
meaning: Practice makes perfect — repetition is what turns clumsy effort into mastery.

text: 三個臭皮匠，頂個諸葛亮
translit: sān gè chòu píjiàng, dǐng gè Zhūgě Liàng
en: Three humble cobblers equal one Zhuge Liang
meaning: Ordinary people thinking together can match the wisdom of a great strategist — collective intelligence beats a single mind.

text: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다
translit: ganeun mari gowaya oneun mari kopta
en: The words you send must be lovely for the words that return to be lovely
meaning: Treat others with kindness and they will treat you the same — courtesy returns to its sender.

text: Ăn quả nhớ kẻ trồng cây
translit: ăn quả nhớ kẻ trồng cây
en: When you eat fruit, remember the one who planted the tree
meaning: Be grateful to those who made your good fortune possible — enjoy the harvest but honour its source.

text: Ở hiền gặp lành
translit: ở hiền gặp lành
en: Live kindly and meet good things
meaning: Good people attract good fortune — kindness is eventually rewarded.

text: น้ำลดตอผุด
translit: nam lot tor phut
en: When the water falls, the stump appears
meaning: When the cover of prosperity or power recedes, the true nature of things — and people — is exposed.

text: Berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing
translit: berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing
en: Heavy together we carry it, light together we haul it
meaning: Shared burdens and joys alike — face life's load and its easy moments together as a community.

text: Bersatu kita teguh, bercerai kita runtuh
translit: bersatu kita teguh, bercerai kita runtuh
en: United we stand firm, divided we collapse
meaning: Strength comes from unity; a group that splits apart grows weak and falls — the same idea as 'unity is strength'.

text: Ang hindi maraho magmahal sa sariling wika, ay mas bahagpa sa hayop at malansang isda
translit: ang hindi maraho magmahal sa sariling wika
en: One who does not love his own language is worse than an animal and a putrid fish
meaning: To neglect your mother tongue is to neglect your own identity — a line from José Rizal, national hero of the Philippines.

text: Bersatu teguh, bercerai runtuh
translit: bersatu teguh bercerai runtuh
en: United we stand firm, divided we fall
meaning: A well-known Malay maxim about the strength of togetherness and the collapse that follows disunity.

text: अब पछताए होत क्या, जब चिरिया फोटै बरिया
translit: ab pachhtāe hot kyā, jab chiriya phuṭai bariyā
en: What use is regret now, when the bird has flown from the trap?
meaning: It is no use crying over spilt milk — repentance after the loss changes nothing.

text: जल में रहकर मगर से दुस्ती
translit: jal meṁ rahkar magar se dustī
en: Living in the water, one must befriend the crocodile
meaning: You must make the best of dangerous company when you cannot escape it — adapt to survive in hostile surroundings.

text: صبر کا پھل میٹھا ہوتا ہے
translit: sabr kā phal mīṭhā hotā hai
en: The fruit of patience is sweet
meaning: Endure now and the reward comes later — patience ripens into something good.

text: دوست دوست کا ہاتھ ہوتا ہے
translit: dost dost kā hāth hotā hai
en: A friend is a friend's (other) hand
meaning: A true friend is your own ability to act — help and loyalty when you need them most.

text: الوقت كالسيف إن لم تقطعه قطعك
translit: al-waqtu ka-s-sayf, in lam taqṭaʿhu qaṭaʿak
en: Time is like a sword: if you do not cut it, it cuts you
meaning: Time is unforgiving — master it or it will waste you.

text: Bir elin nesi var, iki elin sesi var
translit: bir elin nesi var, iki elin sesi var
en: What can one hand do? Two hands make a sound
meaning: One hand alone is silent; two clapping make music — many hands accomplish what one cannot.

text: Damlaya damlaya göl olur
translit: damlaya damlaya göl olur
en: Drop by drop, a lake is formed
meaning: Small savings or efforts, added together, become something large — patience and accumulation win.

text: الصديق وقت الضيق
translit: aṣ-ṣadīqu waqta ḍ-ḍīq
en: A friend is (known) at the time of hardship
meaning: A friend in need is a friend indeed — real friendship is proven in trouble, not in good times.

text: عصفور في اليد خير من عشرة على الشجرة
translit: ʿuṣfūrun fī al-yadi khayrun min ʿashrin ʿalā ash-shajara
en: A bird in the hand is better than ten on the tree
meaning: A small certain possession beats a large uncertain promise — the same wisdom as the English 'bird in the hand'.

text: Haraka haraka haina baraka
translit: haraka haraka haina baraka
en: Hurry hurry has no blessing
meaning: Rushed work lacks blessing — go slowly enough to do it properly.

text: Umoja ni nguvu, utengano ni udhaifu
translit: umoja ni nguvu, utengano ni udhaifu
en: Unity is strength, division is weakness
meaning: Togetherness empowers; splitting apart makes all weak — the Kiswahili anthem of cooperation.

text: Maji yakishamwagika, hayakusanyiki tena
translit: maji yakishamwagika, hayakusanyiki tena
en: Once water is spilled, it cannot be gathered again
meaning: It is no use crying over spilt milk — what is lost cannot be recovered, so move on.

text: A single hand cannot tie a bundle.
translit: aka otu ụgbọ anaghị ekwe ke
en: One hand cannot tie a bundle
meaning: Cooperation is necessary — no one can accomplish a real task alone.

text: When the rain is beating down and the people are crowded under a little shelter, no one can say the rain is gentle.
en: In a shared hardship, no one can claim the storm is mild
meaning: A common crisis felt by all cannot be spun as easy by any one person — trouble levels the group. A traditional Igbo saying popularised by Chinua Achebe.

text: Onipa bi nso ne onipa.
translit: onipa bi nso ne onipa
en: Another person is also a person
meaning: Every other human being is fully a person too — the Akan foundation of empathy, the root of ubuntu.

text: Umntu ngumntu ngabantu.
translit: umntu ngumntu ngabantu
en: A person is a person through other people
meaning: The heart of ubuntu: our humanity is made in community — we exist through and because of one another.

text: Το μέτρον άριστον
translit: to metron ariston
en: The measure — moderation — is best
meaning: Nothing in excess; moderation is the best policy — a core idea of Delphic wisdom.

text: Γνῶθι σεαυτόν
translit: gnōthi seauton
en: Know thyself
meaning: Insight into your own nature is the beginning of wisdom — inscribed at the Temple of Apollo at Delphi.

text: Tempus fugit
translit: tempus fugit
en: Time flies
meaning: Time slips away swiftly — seize the day before the moment is gone. A Roman (Latin) maxim.

text: Errare humanum est
translit: errāre hūmānum est
en: To err is human
meaning: Making mistakes is part of being human — forgiveness and learning follow from that truth.

text: Chi dorme non piglia pesci.
translit: ki ˈdɔrme non ˈpiʎʎa ˈpeʃʃi
en: Whoever sleeps catches no fish
meaning: The early bird gets the worm — idleness wins nothing.

text: Oggi pane, domani pane.
translit: ˈɔddʒi ˈpaːne, doˈmani ˈpaːne
en: Today bread, tomorrow bread
meaning: A monotonous life of the same thing day after day — nothing improves, nothing changes.

text: Reculer pour mieux sauter
translit: ʁəkyle puʁ mjø sote
en: Step back to jump further
meaning: A temporary retreat lets you gather force for a bigger advance — strategy over stubbornness.

text: Qui ne dit mot consent
translit: ki nə di mo kɔ̃sɛ̃t
en: Whoever says nothing consents
meaning: Silence is agreement — if you do not object, it counts as yes.

text: Ordnung muss sein
translit: ˈɔrdnʊŋ mʊs zaɪn
en: There must be order
meaning: Things must be kept tidy and structured — order in life and work is a virtue (famously associated with Kant).

text: Das Ende vom Lied ist immer dasselbe
translit: das ˈɛndə fɔm ˈliːt ɪst ˈɪmɐ dasˈzɛlbə
en: The end of the song is always the same
meaning: No matter how the story starts, it finishes the same way — a weary remark about recurring bad outcomes.

text: Más sabe el diablo por viejo que por diablo
translit: más sabe el diablo por viejo que por diablo
en: The devil knows more because he is old than because he is the devil
meaning: Experience and age bring more wisdom than innate cunning — respect the lessons of years.

text: En boca cerrada no entran moscas
translit: en boca cerrada no entran moscas
en: No flies enter a closed mouth
meaning: Keeping silent keeps you out of trouble — it is safer not to speak needlessly.

text: Para dor aguda, remédio amargo
translit: para dor aguda, remédio amargo
en: For a sharp pain, a bitter cure
meaning: Hard situations call for unpleasant remedies — the medicine you need is rarely sweet.

text: Quem tem boca vai a Roma
translit: quem tem boca vai a roma
en: Whoever has a mouth (can ask the way and) reaches Rome
meaning: A willingness to ask and speak up gets you anywhere — using your voice solves problems.

text: Не родись красивой, а родись счастливой
translit: ne rodis' krasivoy, a rodis' schastlivoy
en: Don't be born beautiful, be born lucky
meaning: Good fortune outweighs good looks — luck in life matters more than appearance.

text: Без труда не вытащишь и рыбку из пруда
translit: bez truda ne vytyashchish i rybku iz pruda
en: Without effort you can't even pull a fish out of a pond
meaning: Nothing comes without work — even the simplest reward demands effort.

text: Ní neart go cur le chéile
translit: nii nyart go cur le kheile
en: There is no strength without coming together
meaning: Unity is strength — real power exists only when people stand together. The motto of the Irish state.

text: Never put off till tomorrow what you can do today.
en: Never postpone to tomorrow what you can do today
meaning: Procrastination is a trap — act now while the moment is yours. Popularised by Lord Chesterfield.

text: A rolling stone gathers no moss.
en: A rolling stone gathers no moss
meaning: One who keeps moving takes no root — read either as a warning against restlessness or a praise of constant activity.

text: Nie wszystko złoto, co się świeci.
translit: ɲɛ ˈfʂɨst͡skɔ ˈzwɔtɔ t͡sɔ ɕɛ ˈɕfɲɛt͡ɕi
en: Not all that glitters is gold
meaning: Appearances can deceive — something shiny is not always valuable or true.

text: Jak Kuba Bogu, tak Bóg Kubie.
translit: jak kuba bogu tak bug kubie
en: As Kuba treats God, so God treats Kuba
meaning: You get back exactly what you give — what goes around comes around.

text: Boven de wolken zitten.
translit: ˌboːvə(n) də ˈʋɔlkə(n) ˈzɪtə(n)
en: To sit above the clouds
meaning: To be extremely cheerful or content — over the moon, with a lightness untouched by the weather.

text: Kdo jinému jámu kopá, sám do ní padá.
translit: kdo jinemu jamu kopa, sam do ni pada
en: Whoever digs a pit for another falls into it himself
meaning: The schemes you make against others will likely trap you — the same teaching as the biblical 'do not dig a pit'.

text: Lagom är bäst.
translit: ˈlɑːɡɔm ær bɛst
en: 'Just the right amount' is best
meaning: The Swedish ideal of moderation — not too much, not too little; 'just right' is the finest.

text: Man skal ikke glæde sig, før man er kommen over broen.
translit: man skal ikke glæde sig før man er kommen over broen
en: Do not rejoice before you have crossed the bridge
meaning: Don't count your chickens before they hatch — celebrate only once the outcome is secured.

text: Det er ikke gull alt som glimter.
translit: deːt ɛr ˈikːə ɡʉl alə sm ˈɡlɪmːtə
en: Not all that glitters is gold
meaning: Shiny things are not always genuine — appearances deceive, the Norse form of a universal warning.

text: Água mole em pedra dura, tanto bate até que fura.
translit: ˈaɡwa ˈmɔli ẽj ˈpɛdɾa ˈduɾa, ˈtɐ̃tu ˈbatʃi aˈtɛ ki ˈfuɾa
en: Soft water on hard stone beats until it pierces
meaning: Persistence wears down the hardest obstacle — steady repetition breaks stone.

text: Al mal tiempo, buena cara.
translit: al mal ˈjjempo ˈbwe-na ˈka-ra
en: In bad weather, keep a good face
meaning: Meet hardship with a cheerful attitude — you cannot always change circumstances, but you can meet them well.

text: El que a buen árbol se arrima, buena sombra le cobija.
translit: el ke a ˈβwen ˈaɾ-βol se aˈri-ma ˈbwe-na ˈsom-bɾa le ko-ˈβi-xa
en: Whoever leans on a good tree, good shade shelters him
meaning: Attach yourself to good people and they will protect and lift you — the worth of your associations shapes your life.

text: Al que no le gusta el caldo, que no se meta a cocinero.
translit: al ke no le ˈɣus-ta el ˈkal-do ke no se ˈme-ta a ko-si-ˈne-ɾo
en: Whoever does not like the broth should not become a cook
meaning: Do not take up a role whose burdens you dislike — accept the real cost of your choices.

text: El que no tiene candela, que prenda en la del vecino.
translit: el ke no ˈtie-ne kan-ˈde-la ke ˈpren-da en la del be-ˈsi-no
en: Whoever has no fire should light it from the neighbour's
meaning: When you lack something, borrow and share — resourcefulness and community solve want.

text: She'll be right, mate.
en: It will be all right in the end
meaning: The easy-going Australian assurance that things sort themselves out — relaxed optimism in the face of trouble.

text: Ka whawhai tonu mātou, Ake! Ake! Ake!
translit: ka fa-fai to-noo maa-too a-ke a-ke a-ke
en: We will fight on, forever and ever
meaning: Unyielding perseverance — a Māori saying of tenacity: 'we will not give in', to the very end.

text: He waka eke noa.
translit: he wa-ka e-ke no-a
en: It is a canoe we are all aboard
meaning: We are all in this together — a shared journey demands that everyone paddles, an idea of collective responsibility.
